description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between accuracy (ACC, in percentage) and co-occurrence number for five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME—across a range of co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is plotted on a logarithmic scale, spanning from 1 to 1000, with tick marks at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is linear and ranges from 60 to 85, with major gridlines at 65, 70, 75, and 80. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circular markers, showing a steady increase in accuracy from approximately 64% at a co-occurrence number of 1 to about 71% at 1000. The "MEND" method, depicted with a brown line and diamond markers, starts at around 70.5% and rises to approximately 80% at the highest co-occurrence number. The "FT" method, shown with a blue line and triangle markers, begins at about 65.5% and increases to roughly 73% at the end of the range. The "MEMIT" method, represented by a purple line with diamond markers, starts at approximately 69.5% and climbs to about 77.5%. Finally, the "ROME" method, shown with a green line and square markers, begins at around 74% and increases to a peak of approximately 83.5% at the highest co-occurrence number. All methods exhibit a general upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
